Classic Android firmware on a modern phone
The system and all data inside it will be deleted (%1$s). The shared memory card folder stays.
Allow access to all files: then each system’s memory card lives in the AEmulator folder of internal storage — handy for APKs, music and photos.
Add an ARM firmware for Android 2.2–6.0: a recovery ZIP, an Odin archive (.tar.md5), system.img or a factory image.
Android 2.x uses a fixed 480×800 screen at 240 dpi.
A smaller screen makes the system faster.
Hardware graphics through the GL bridge. Turn off if the picture breaks.
Smoother, but some firmware shows artifacts.
Faster; without it fussy firmware is more reliable.
The older Desire HD engine: GLES 1.x only, 480×800 screen. Use it if the main engine fails.
Lets old browsers and apps open today’s HTTPS sites.
Back, Home, Recents and Menu under the screen.
For firmware that doesn’t understand multitouch.
The first boot takes longer: the system optimizes apps.
Pick any color to restyle the whole app
Applied to every firmware you import from now on
Creator of the Desire HD and One M7 emulators this project grew from
AEmulator runs classic Android firmware on modern phones. Free and open source.
What the status bar shows: 2G to LTE. Default 2G, since not every firmware handles 3G or newer
Telephony, IMEI and signal. Off: the firmware behaves like a Wi-Fi tablet
Shown in /proc/version and uname -r (e.g. 3.0.31-custom, or a full "Linux version ..." line). Applied on next boot. Blank = default
Reported as gsm.version.baseband and by the modem. Applied on next boot. Blank = default
Reported as ro.serialno and ro.boot.serialno (letters and digits, up to 32). Applied on next boot. Blank = default
Example: -d unimp DHD_TBFLUSH=2 (NAME=value becomes an environment variable)
Service names separated by commas, e.g. mediaserver,zygote. Slows those services down and writes the trace to their logs. Applies at the next boot.
Shows the host\'s internet to the VM as a connected Wi-Fi network instead of Ethernet. Android 4.0–7.x. Applies at the next boot.
The network name cannot be empty
Leave empty for an open network. WPA2 needs 8–63 characters.
Use 8–63 characters, or leave empty for an open network

Value of ro.hardware given to the guest at launch. The system looks up HAL libraries by it (gralloc.<value>.so, lights.<value>.so…), so change it only if you know what the firmware expects. Takes effect after a full VM restart.
Reboot to it from the ⋮ menu. A recovery.img of TWRP, OrangeFox or CWM can replace it.
Install delta OTA image on top of this system image
An incremental update zip. Its metadata is checked against this system’s build.prop before anything is changed.

This system:
%1$s

will be updated to:
%2$s

The VM’s /system and boot ramdisk are patched and its dalvik cache is cleared; apps and data are kept. If anything does not match, nothing is changed.

Warning: this system has only a build thumbprint, not a full fingerprint. Only the Android version, build ID, incremental, build type and signing keys were compared; manufacturer, product and model could not be verified. Continue anyway?
Updated to %1$s (%2$d files patched, %3$d added, %4$d removed).
Root shell of the firmware. Type a command (e.g. ls /sdcard, getprop, pm list packages).
Anyone on this Wi-Fi network gets a root shell of the firmware. Switch it off on public networks.
ZIP, TAR/MD5, IMG, TWRP & CWM backups
Another copy of a firmware you have: own apps, data, card and settings
The container is a full separate copy of the firmware, /system included: flashing or changing one never affects the other. /data starts clean unless copied.
ART compiles apps to machine code: first boot and installs take much longer, apps run faster
Check GitHub for new releases on app startup
A new version %1$s is available. Would you like to update?

HAL1 ROMs: 640×480 preview and photos, rear/front camera. Requires permission and a full VM restart. Camera closes when AEmulator is backgrounded; reopen the guest camera app. Video is recorded at 640×480.
Camera permission denied. The ROM will boot without host-camera access; grant permission in Android app settings and fully restart the VM to retry.
Mark setup complete and disable recognized setup apps on next full boot. Turning off does not reset completed setup. OEM support may vary.
HTTP or HTTPS URL. HTTPS is recommended.
ROM compatibility statuses are not verified by the app.
ROM download URL isn\'t available right now.
Invalid or incomplete catalog data on lines: %1$s
No browser is available to open this link.
Could not restart the emulator. Close this screen and open the firmware again.
VM storage is busy. Wait for data reset to finish, then try again.

Shut down the VM first. Permanently delete guest apps, accounts, settings and internal data (/data and /cache)? No backup is created. Firmware, VM settings, recovery and the shared SD-card folder are kept.
VM data permanently reset. No backup was created.
Cannot complete reset. Fully shut down all VMs and check the image files. If deletion started, some data may already be permanently erased.
Stop all VMs first. Choose what to include. Shared SD-card files are not included.
Includes guest apps, accounts and private files. Only share this archive with people you trust.
Exporting VM… Please keep this screen open.
VM exported. Use Import firmware to restore the .aessvm file.
Export failed. Fully shut down all VMs and check destination space and access. If a partial file remains, delete it before retrying.

Forward available accelerometer, gyroscope and magnetic-field sensors (Android 2.2–7.1). When off, Rotate screen simulates gravity instead; guest auto-rotate must be enabled. Experimental; takes effect after a full VM restart. Paused while the VM screen is hidden.

0° / 180° pins the host motion sensors to a fixed orientation: gravity stays put and the gyroscope reads zero, so the guest never auto-rotates. No gyroscope hides the gyroscope from the guest completely (use it if the gyro misbehaves); accelerometer and magnetometer stay real. Takes effect after a full VM restart.

Use the physical host display size and density after a full VM restart. Emulator controls overlay the guest. The cutout barrier is in app settings. High resolutions require more RAM and rendering time. The legacy 2.x engine keeps its fixed resolution.
Keep the VM screen clear of the notch or camera cutout. Off allows fullscreen behind it. Applies when reopening a VM.
Guest Android could not rotate the screen. Check the VM logs.

After a full restart, disable detected Google apps, Play Store, Play services and Google account components. Keep launchers, keyboards, WebView and critical system components. Setup wizard is controlled separately. Apps that need Google services may stop working. Turning this off restores only apps disabled by this option; APKs and app data are not deleted.
Phone rotation simulated. Enable auto-rotate in guest Android.
Export the firmware and any available boot files together. Without this, the archive cannot create a new VM.
Include VM settings for restoration or Import settings. ROM identity is kept even when settings are excluded.
Settings loaded. Press Save to apply. System, boot and data are unchanged.

Archive: %1$s
This VM: %2$s

The device/ROM differs, or its identity cannot be verified. These settings may not suit this VM. Import settings anyway? Partitions will not be imported.
Reading boot partition… Stop all VMs before importing.
Boot partition imported. The boot plan was refreshed; system and data are unchanged.
Reading OEM partition… Stop all VMs before importing.
OEM partition imported and mounted at /oem. System and data are unchanged.
Follow the tablet window rotation. Off keeps controls on the device’s natural bottom edge. Does not follow motion when host auto-rotate is off. Guest screen is never rotated or stretched by the host.

Reported chipset: %1$s

Your chipset’s compatibility is unverified. If a VM won’t boot, try disabling JIT and/or the GPU bridge in VM settings before reporting it. A boot failure alone on an unverified chipset does not establish an emulator bug.

Chipset detection can be incomplete, especially on older Android versions. Recognizing Snapdragon, Dimensity or Google Tensor does not guarantee that every ROM will boot. If you still report an issue, include the chipset, ROM details and VM logs.
The update file (%1$s) has been downloaded. Tap “Install” to update the app.
Shown until Android boots and stays running for 10 seconds.
Match your device’s battery level and charging state.
Off: the slot is empty and the firmware shows \"No SIM card\". Applies at the next boot.
A real network, or type the codes below. ✓ = this firmware has mobile data settings (APN) for it
The MCC has 3 digits, the MNC 2 or 3
This firmware has no mobile data settings (APN) for this operator, so mobile data may not connect. Calls, SMS and Wi-Fi are not affected.
Shown in Settings › About phone › Status
A second fake SIM. Only firmware built for two SIMs uses it (many Samsung and MediaTek ones). Applies at the next boot.
The Wi-Fi list also shows a few other networks (locked, they cannot be joined)
The VM hears the microphone of this phone (voice recorders, video sound) while it is on screen. Off: recordings are silent. Applies at the next boot.
Microphone permission denied: the VM records silence. Grant it in Android app settings and fully restart the VM to retry.
Tap the phone to turn it over
Navigation bar keys, colours and the frame around the guest screen, styled after an Android era or your own design.
Themes change only the app around the VM; the firmware is never modified. Changes apply when a VM screen is opened again.
A soft light behind a pressed key (Honeycomb, Holo, Lollipop) instead of a filled box
The faint glow of the Android 3.x and 4.x system bars
Off: a flat bar from edge to edge, like real phones
With the GPU bridge on, some phones do not round the corners of the guest screen.
How the app itself looks. Changes apply right away.
Black background in the dark theme, for OLED screens
Turn off for calmer, standard motion
This is how cards, buttons and text look now.
A custom accent color is set and takes priority. Reset it to see this theme.
